AbstractText.Label: BACKGROUND
AbstractText.content: Treatment of acute agitation in patients with bipolar disorder and schizophrenia is a multifaceted and dynamic task, which presents unique and complex challenges to healthcare providers.

AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: To ascertain and describe which medications are best to use in agitated patients with schizophrenia or bipolar disorder Method: Selective review of current guidelines and of the literature pertaining to the treatment of agitation in patients with schizophrenia or bipolar disorder Results: Pharmacologic treatment of agitation should be based on an assessment of the most likely cause of the agitation. The use for treatment of acute agitation in patients with schizophrenia and bipolar disease of a variety of first-generation antipsychotic drugs, second-generation antipsychotic drugs, benzodiazepines and the newer inhaled antipsychotic loxapine, is reviewed and commented.

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: It is recommended that the mainstay of pharmacological treatment of agitation be based on an assessment of its most likely cause. If agitation is due to delirium or to another medical condition, clinicians should first attempt to address and treat the underlying cause. When agitation is primarily due to schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, antipsychotics and/or benzodiazepines are usually the mainstay of treatment. Newer inhaled formulation of loxapine has shown ability to rapidly reduce the agitation in mild to moderate patients with schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, with a decrease in agitation that was evident since the first assessment, 10 minutes after the first dose.
